mainTopic: Two deeds for the same property: same-day deeds (רב vs. שמואל, רבי מאיר vs. רבי אלעזר, שודא דדייני) and deeds with exact vs. vague dates
overview: The amud opens by finishing a suggestion: רב, who says two same-day deeds are split, follows רבי מאיר, for whom the signing witnesses make a deed take effect. שמואל, who leaves it to the judges (שודא דדייני), follows רבי אלעזר, for whom the delivery witnesses make it take effect. The גמרא tries saying that both follow רבי אלעזר and argue only about how to settle doubt. It rejects that, because רב is known to apply רבי אלעזר only to גיטין. A ברייתא that says 'they divide' is used to challenge שמואל. The first answer, that it follows רבי מאיר, fails because of the ברייתא's last clause. So the גמרא says splitting versus discretion is its own argument among the תנאים. Next comes the story of רמי בר חמא's mother, who wrote her property to two sons on one day. רב נחמן defends ruling by שודא דדייני against רב ששת's 'the earlier deed wins.' Finally, רב יוסף rules that a deed dated the fifth of ניסן beats one dated only 'ניסן.' The losing party then starts a request that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the suggestion: שמואל follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proposed explanation. If רב follows רבי מאיר, then שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, who says the delivery witnesses make a document effective.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל, who ruled the way he did, follows רבי אלעזר, who says: the witnesses who see the document handed over are what make it take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a 'shall we say' suggestion it began just before this section. It now explains שמואל's side: he follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says a document takes effect when it is handed over in front of witnesses, not when it is signed. So two deeds with the same date were almost surely handed over at different times, and only one buyer really owns the field. That is why שמואל will not simply split it.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who watch the document being handed over
They 'cut', meaning they make the document legally take effect
The תנא who says delivery, not signing, makes a document effective

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new opinion. It is the second half of a suggestion that began earlier: 'Shall we say רב follows רבי מאיר (signing witnesses) and שמואל follows רבי אלעזר (delivery witnesses)?'

phrases.english: And Shmuel, who ruled as he did, holds like Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: שמואל's ruling was that with two deeds dated the same day, the judges decide who gets the field.

phrases.english: who said: the witnesses of the handing-over make it take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proposal begun just before this section, which linked רב to רבי מאיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רב and שמואל really the old argument between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר about which witnesses make a document effective?

steps.title: No: both follow רבי אלעזר and argue about how to handle doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe everyone agrees with רבי אלעזר, and the real argument is what to do when we cannot know who received his deed first: split it, or let the judges decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really everyone follows רבי אלעזר. Here they argue about this: רב thinks splitting is better, and שמואל thinks leaving it to the judges' judgment is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that רב and שמואל are repeating the רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר argument. It offers another way to understand their disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי אלעזר, one buyer really did get the deed first, but we do not know which one. So the question becomes how a בית דין handles an unsolvable money doubt. רב says split it (חלוקה), and שמואל says the judges use their judgment (שודא דדייני).

keyTerms.meaning: The judges' own discretion in deciding who gets it

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that two אמוראים can agree on the basic rule and still argue about how a court settles a doubt it cannot resolve.

phrases.english: No, everyone holds like Rabbi Elazar,
and here they disagree about this:
Rav holds: dividing is better.
And Shmuel holds: the judges' discretion is better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed linking of רב and שמואל to the רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the argument depends on רבי מאיר versus רבי אלעזר; it does not reject either ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is another way to explain the argument: it is about the best way to settle doubt, not about which witnesses make the document effective.

steps.title: Challenge: רב does not follow רבי אלעזר for regular documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב could follow רבי אלעזר. רב יהודה reported that רב follows רבי אלעזר only for גיטין, and שמואל added 'even for documents.' That means רב himself did not apply it to documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say רב follows רבי אלעזר? But רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the law follows רבי אלעזר for divorce documents. When I said this before שמואל, he said: even for other documents. This shows that רב holds it does not apply to other documents!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation from step 2, which said that even רב follows רבי אלעזר. It brings a report showing that רב limited רבי אלעזר's rule to גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's reply was 'even for documents.' That reply only makes sense if רב had not included ordinary documents. So for deeds like the ones in our case, רב does not follow רבי אלעזר, and step 2 cannot be right about רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really explain it this way?
Other legal documents, such as deeds

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַב כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר?
phrases.english: But can you really explain Rav as holding like Rabbi Elazar?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Elazar regarding bills of divorce.
When I said it in front of Shmuel,
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, who was a student of both רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: he said: even regarding other documents.
This implies that Rav holds: regarding documents, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַב כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 2 that רב follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'everyone,' including רב, follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own ruling, as seen from שמואל's 'even for documents,' limits רבי אלעזר's rule to גיטין. So for deeds, רב does not follow רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Conclusion: רב follows רבי מאיר, שמואל follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Since the other approach failed, the גמרא concludes that the first suggestion was right: רב follows רבי מאיר and שמואל follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: רב follows רבי מאיר, and שמואל follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the explanation from step 2 and returns to the original suggestion. Now it states it as clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב follows רבי מאיר, so the deeds took effect when they were signed. Both were signed the same day, so both buyers have an equal claim and they split the field. שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, so only the one handed over first counts, and since we do not know which one that was, the judges decide.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear, the plain conclusion
The תנא who holds that the signing witnesses make a document effective (עדי חתימה כרתי)

steps.whatToRemember: רב (split) = רבי מאיר, signing witnesses make the document effective. שמואל (judges decide) = רבי אלעזר, delivery witnesses make it effective.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: Rav holds like Rabbi Meir,
and Shmuel holds like Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in step 3 and goes back to the suggestion in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument between רב and שמואל matches the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר about which witnesses make a document take effect.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל from a ברייתא that says 'they divide'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: two deeds issued on the same day, the buyers split the field. This looks like a direct refutation of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: two deeds issued on one day, the buyers divide. This refutes שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks שמואל using a ברייתא that rules exactly like רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא is not supposed to argue with a ברייתא. A ברייתא that says 'divide' seems to show that שמואל's ruling, leaving it to the judges, is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised a challenge from a תנאי source

phrases.english: They raised an objection: two documents
that come out dated on one day, they divide,
a refutation of Shmuel!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: שְׁנֵי שְׁטָרוֹת הַיּוֹצְאִים בְּיוֹם אֶחָד חוֹלְקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that each אמורא is tied to a תנא, the גמרא tests שמואל against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the judges decide.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly rules that the buyers divide, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל answers: that ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל can say that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and he himself rules like רבי אלעזר. So the ברייתא does not bind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל would tell you: whose view is this? It is רבי מאיר's, and I ruled like רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by saying the ברייתא follows the other תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling 'divide' fits רבי מאיר, because for him both deeds took effect at signing on the same day. An אמורא may follow one תנא against another. So שמואל, following רבי אלעזר, is not refuted.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא's first defense of שמואל is that the 'divide' ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. Don't lock this in yet: the next step challenges it from the ברייתא's own last clause, and step 8 gives a different answer.

phrases.english: Shmuel could say to you:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir's,
and I ruled like Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against שמואל in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא (רבי מאיר) whom שמואל does not follow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא states the law for everyone, so it refutes שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר only. שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, so his ruling still stands.

steps.title: The last clause of the ברייתא does not fit רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, why does its last clause say that the person who was handed the deed acquires? רבי מאיר holds that the signing witnesses make the deed work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, look at its last part: if someone wrote a deed for one person and handed it to another, the one who was handed it acquires. But if it is רבי מאיר, why does he acquire? רבי מאיר said the signing witnesses are what make a deed work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 6, which said the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. The end of that same ברייתא clearly does not sound like רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, a deed takes effect through the witnesses who signed it, so the person whose name is written in it should own the property. The ברייתא says the person who was physically handed the deed acquires. That is the view of רבי אלעזר, who holds that the witnesses who see the handing over make it work. So the ברייתא cannot be רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Read the last part (of the same source)
The witnesses who sign the document
Make it work, give the document its legal force

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two תנאים. For רבי מאיר, the signatures do the work. For רבי אלעזר, the handing over in front of witnesses does the work.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir, say the latter clause:
If he wrote it for one person and handed it to another,
the one he handed it to has acquired.
But if it is Rabbi Meir, why did he acquire?
Didn't he say that the signing witnesses make it take effect!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 6, which said the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא about two deeds follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause gives the field to the person who received the deed. Only רבי אלעזר holds that way, so the ברייתא cannot be רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Splitting versus leaving it to the judges is a separate argument between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The whole ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר. The question of splitting versus leaving it to the judges is its own argument between תנאים, as a ברייתא about money sent with a messenger shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: the חכמים say they should divide it, and here they said the third party may do whatever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר after all. Some תנאים say to split, and other תנאים say to let someone decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So שמואל can still follow רבי אלעזר. He simply sides with the תנאים who leave it to the judges instead of splitting. The ברייתא that says to split follows other תנאים who hold like רבי אלעזר too. As proof that such an argument exists, the גמרא brings a case where the חכמים say to split and others let the third party decide. That third-party approach is like letting the judges decide.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among the תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer for שמואל: he follows רבי אלעזר. The ברייתא that says to split follows a different opinion among the תנאים on what to do when the order is unclear.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tannaim.
As it is taught: And the Sages say: They should divide it,
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes only the end of this ברייתא. It is about money sent with a messenger, where the sender and the receiver both died.

phrases.english: and here they said:
Whatever the third party wants, he may do.
phrases.notes: The third party is the messenger who is holding the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 7 by moving the ברייתא over to רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the source to a different תנא and shows a separate argument among the תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא that says to split had to follow רבי מאיר, so it did not bind שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר. Splitting versus letting someone decide is a separate argument among the תנאים, and שמואל picks the 'let them decide' side.

steps.title: A mother gives her property to two sons on the same day
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא's mother wrote her property to him in the morning, and in the evening she wrote it to his brother מר עוקבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא's mother wrote her property over to רמי בר חמא in the morning. In the evening she wrote it over to מר עוקבא בר חמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a real-life story about two deeds written for the same property on the same day. This step sets up the case, and the rulings come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we know exactly which deed came first: the morning one. It is a real test of the questions the sugya has been discussing about two deeds for one property.

phrases.english: The mother of Rami bar Chama

phrases.aramaic: כְּתַבְתִּינְהוּ לְנִכְסַהּ לְרָמִי בַּר חָמָא בְּצַפְרָא,
phrases.english: wrote her property over to Rami bar Chama in the morning;

phrases.aramaic: לְאוּרְתָּא כְּתַבְתִּינְהוּ לְמָר עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא.
phrases.english: in the evening she wrote it over to Mar Ukva bar Chama.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory of two deeds to a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: two deeds for the same property, one in the morning and one in the evening.

steps.title: Two judges rule for two different brothers
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gave the property to רמי בר חמא, and רב נחמן gave it to מר עוקבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא came before רב ששת, and רב ששת put him in possession of the property. מר עוקבא came before רב נחמן, and רב נחמן put him in possession of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: Each brother goes to a different judge, and each judge rules for the brother who came to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two rulings that clash over the same property. The story does not yet tell us why each judge ruled the way he did. That is what the next step asks.

keyTerms.meaning: He put him in possession of the property
Before him (to bring a case to a judge)

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama came before Rav Sheshet,
and he established him in the property.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא מָר עוּקְבָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Mar Ukva came before Rav Nachman,
and he established him in the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 9 with the two rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת ruled for the morning deed. רב נחמן ruled for the evening deed.

steps.title: Each judge asks the other for his reason
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks רב נחמן why he ruled that way, and רב נחמן answers with the same question back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת came before רב נחמן and said to him: What is the reason you did this? רב נחמן said to him: And what is the reason you did that?
steps.whatsHappening: The two judges meet, and each one asks the other to explain his ruling. This sets up the reasons that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן does not answer right away. He turns the question around, so רב ששת has to defend his own ruling first. Each side's reasoning comes after this.

keyTerms.meaning: Did the Master (you) act this way

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet came before Rav Nachman

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא עֲבַד מָר הָכִי?
phrases.english: and said to him: What is the reason the Master acted this way?
phrases.notes: "The Master" is a polite way of saying "you".

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמַאי טַעְמָא עֲבַד מָר הָכִי?
phrases.english: He said to him: And what is the reason the Master acted this way?
phrases.notes: Now רב נחמן is asking רב ששת about his ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The two judges who gave the clashing rulings in Step 10 now ask each other for their reasons.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind each judge's ruling

steps.title: רב ששת: The earlier deed wins
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains he gave the property to רמי בר חמא because his deed came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because it came first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives his reason: רמי בר חמא's deed was written in the morning, before מר עוקבא's deed in the evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's logic is simple: once the mother gave the property away in the morning, she no longer owned it in the evening. So the second deed should give nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: because it came first (it was earlier)

phrases.english: He said to him: Because it came first.
phrases.notes: This is רב ששת speaking, answering the question from the last step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why רב ששת ruled as he did.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רב ששת give the property to רמי בר חמא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because his deed was written earlier in the day.

steps.title: רב נחמן: We don't write hours on deeds here
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects that outside ירושלים deeds do not list the hour, so morning and evening on the same day count as the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are we sitting in ירושלים, where we write the hours?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב ששת's reason. He says that where they live, deeds only record the day and not the hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hour is not written in the deed, the deed cannot prove which one came first within a single day. So legally both deeds carry the same date, and 'it came first' does not decide anything.

keyTerms.meaning: is it so that...? (a word that opens a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: He said to him:
Are we sitting in Jerusalem,
phrases.notes: In ירושלים, deeds wrote down the exact hour. Elsewhere they only wrote the day.

phrases.english: that we write the hours?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the morning deed wins because it came first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Deeds here record only the day and not the hour. So two deeds from the same day are legally simultaneous, and neither one counts as 'first'.

steps.title: רב ששת asks רב נחמן for his reason
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks: if the deeds are simultaneous, why did you give the property to מר עוקבא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what is the reason the Master did this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת accepts the point about hours, so he turns the question around. If neither deed is first, what made רב נחמן choose מר עוקבא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both deeds have equal standing, there seems to be no basis for picking one brother over the other. רב ששת wants to hear what reason רב נחמן is relying on.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master (a respectful way to say 'you')

phrases.english: But the Master, what is the reason
that he did this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָר מַאי טַעְמָא עֲבַד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב נחמן's objection by asking him to explain his own ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was רב נחמן's basis for giving the property to מר עוקבא?

steps.title: רב נחמן: The judges' discretion
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he ruled by שודא דדייני, the judge's own sense of what the giver wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The discretion of the judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains that when the evidence is equal, the judge is allowed to decide based on his own judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the two deeds are legally equal, the case cannot be settled by dates. In that kind of case the judge may award the property to whoever he senses the giver really meant to have it, and רב נחמן felt that was מר עוקבא.

keyTerms.meaning: the judges' discretion (the judge decides based on his sense of what is right)

steps.whyThisMatters: שודא דדייני is a well-known principle. When the legal evidence on both sides is truly equal, the decision is left to the judge's judgment.

phrases.english: He said to him: The discretion of the judges.
phrases.notes: Literally 'the throwing of the judges': the judge 'throws' the property to whichever side he thinks the giver favored.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He ruled by שודא דדייני, judging what the mother most likely wanted.

steps.title: רב ששת: I used the judges' discretion too
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת claims that his own ruling for רמי בר חמא can also count as שודא דדייני.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I also used the discretion of the judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת pushes back. If discretion decides the case, his ruling should be just as valid as רב נחמן's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Discretion lets a judge go either way. So רב ששת argues his choice of רמי בר חמא is equally legitimate, and there is no reason to prefer רב נחמן's choice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא נָמֵי שׁוּדָא דְּדַיָּינֵי,
phrases.english: He said to him: I too, the discretion of the judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא נָמֵי שׁוּדָא דְּדַיָּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב נחמן's own principle to defend רב ששת's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that his ruling stands because of שודא דדייני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the judge's discretion decides, then רב ששת's ruling is also an act of discretion and should be equally valid.

steps.title: רב נחמן's two reasons his ruling stands
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that only an appointed judge may use שודא דדייני, and that רב ששת did not originally rule for that reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: One, I am a judge and the Master is not a judge. And also, from the start you did not come to it on this basis.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives two answers to show that רב ששת cannot claim to have used discretion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the power of discretion belongs to an official judge, and רב ששת did not hold that position. Second, רב ששת's ruling was based on his reason that the morning deed came first, which turned out to be wrong. He cannot switch to a new reason after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: on this basis, for this reason

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's ruling for מר עוקבא stands. Same-day deeds without hours are equal, and an appointed judge may decide the case by שודא דדייני.

phrases.english: He said to him: One,
that I am a judge
and the Master is not a judge.
And furthermore, from the start,
you did not come to it on this basis.
phrases.notes: He means: you ruled because you thought the morning deed came first, not because of the judges' discretion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדָא, דַּאֲנָא דַּיָּינָא וּמָר לָאו דַּיָּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's attempt to claim the judges' discretion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two separate answers: one about who may use discretion, and one about what the ruling was actually based on.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ruling could be justified afterward as the judges' discretion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an appointed judge who actually ruled on that basis can rely on שודא דדייני.

steps.title: רב יוסף: A specific date beats a general month
steps.stepSummary: Two deeds came before רב יוסף, one dated the fifth of ניסן and one dated only 'ניסן.' He gave the property to the holder of the fifth-of-ניסן deed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two deeds came before רב יוסף. One was written on the fifth of ניסן, and in the other was written just 'ניסן.' רב יוסף put the one with the fifth of ניסן in possession of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about two conflicting deeds for the same property, and how רב יוסף ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the deeds are not from the same day. One gives an exact date, and the other only names the month. רב יוסף gives the property to the deed with the exact date.

keyTerms.meaning: he established him, put him in possession

phrases.english: There were these two deeds
that came before Rav Yosef.
One was written on the fifth of Nisan,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד הֲוָה כָּתוּב בֵּיהּ בְּנִיסָן סְתָמָא.
phrases.english: and in the other was written 'in Nisan,' with no day given.
Rav Yosef established
the one with the fifth of Nisan in the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ תְּרֵי שְׁטָרֵי דַּאֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about two conflicting deeds, following the story of רמי בר חמא and מר עוקבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one deed has an exact date and the other names only the month, the deed with the exact date wins.

steps.title: The other claimant protests
steps.stepSummary: The holder of the undated deed complains: why should I lose, when my deed might be earlier?
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one said to him: And should I lose?
steps.whatsHappening: The man who lost objects to רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His deed says only 'ניסן,' so it might have been written on the first through the fourth, before the other deed. He argues that a mere doubt should not cost him the property.

phrases.english: The other one said to him:
And should I lose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's award of the property to the fifth-of-ניסן deed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The undated deed could just as easily be earlier, so why should its holder lose?

steps.title: רב יוסף: You are at a disadvantage
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the holder of the vague deed has the weaker position, since his deed could be from as late as the twenty-ninth of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Your hand is on the bottom. I can say you are from the twenty-ninth of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why the man with the vague deed loses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vague deed proves only that it was written sometime in ניסן, which could be the end of the month. Since he cannot prove his deed is earlier than the fifth, the deed with the clear date wins.

keyTerms.meaning: your hand is on the bottom, meaning you have the weaker position
I can say, it is possible to say

steps.whatToRemember: A deed with an exact date beats a deed that names only the month. The vague deed is treated as possibly the latest date it could be.

phrases.english: He said to him:
You, your hand is on the bottom,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא בַּר עֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בְּנִיסָן אַתְּ.
phrases.english: I can say you are from the twenty-ninth of Nisan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the losing claimant's protest.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Burden of proof: the party with the vaguer document gets the weaker assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the undated deed might be earlier, the two deeds should be treated as equal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The undated deed may be from the end of the month, so it cannot beat a deed with a clear earlier date.

steps.title: The losing party asks רב יוסף to write something for him
steps.stepSummary: After losing, the holder of the vague 'ניסן' deed turns to רב יוסף and starts a request: 'Let the Master write for me...'
steps.simpleTranslation: He (the man with the vague deed) said to him (רב יוסף): Let the Master write for me...
steps.whatsHappening: The man who lost the case is asking רב יוסף to write him a document. This line is a setup: the גמרא is getting ready to tell us exactly what he wants written and how רב יוסף answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, רב יוסף said the vague deed is weaker because it might be from late in ניסן. The man does not argue with that. Instead he asks the court to write something for him. The sentence is not finished here, so we wait for the next words to see what he is asking for.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him. Here it is the losing party speaking to רב יוסף.
Let (him) write for me. A polite request for a written document.
Master. A respectful way of addressing a חכם, here רב יוסף.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the Master write for me
phrases.notes: The man with the vague 'ניסן' deed is talking to רב יוסף. What he wants written comes in the next line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף explains why the vague deed loses (step 20), the losing party responds with a follow-up request instead of a further protest.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The losing party is asking רב יוסף to write a document for him. The exact content of the request continues in the next line of the גמרא.
